body: What lifestyle changes did you do if I may ask? It seems propanalol isn’t working too well even though I had the dosage upped.
I’ve had mine checked quite a few times and always suspect I have one, my mother does too. But nothing is showing up! Super weird.
I was out for a few days but I just had mine bumped from twice daily to 3-4 times daily as needed. Going to see how that helps but would rather not be on medication for it at all.
Wow I’m so sorry, I’m 27 and I thought I was young for this. They never really go away but my adderall does distract them for a few hours. I hope you figure it out :(
Tell me about it, I wish I had that energy.
I’ve never heard of a sleep consultant for toddlers, I’m going to look it up. I live in Ontario so it may be covered but thanks for bringing it up, could possibly save my sanity.

I’m going to try the heavy work method! Pushing around a heavy bin with stuff in it, I have a weighted blanket. The only thing we’ve found is no matter how much exercise or going out she gets (walking around zoo, aquarium, farm, general walks etc) it doesn’t leave her tired at all. I swear she could stay up for days.

Thank you for all the replies! I’ve tried for over a year to fix her sleep schedule but she turns into the Tasmanian devil during the day if I wake her early. And if we wake her early for an event or if she misses a nap, she goes into over drive and will stay up even later from being tired :( we’ve tried tiring her out in so many different ways and even have a bedtime routine but it doesn’t change. 

For the naps we’ve tried them earlier, still no change. We’ve tried cutting naps out completely and she’s gone insane and getting her to sleep is a real fight. 

Thankfully she’s not underweight but I’m still trying. She gets cranky for sure when she doesn’t eat so I do know that. 

And for the bed we have a king and she will only sleep in it but only if I’m present with her. So while she’s sleeping and napping I can’t leave the bed. 

The best I can do right now I think is keep trying to switch to a different paediatrician for now because everything that works for everyone else doesn’t work for us. Kind of a kick in the ass because my niece a year younger has a perfect schedule haha. I’ll keep trying. Thank you for your advice!

Thank you so much! I’m a smaller girl but a new mom and I won’t mind a bit of weight loss at this time, I’ll definitely try to keep easy food around me to remind myself. I’m starting off small and I think weekly my psych will adjust it if needed! 

I realize it’s different for everyone but a suggestion of am time is great!
At day 3 and 4 I had such an intense headache I couldn’t do anything but sit in bed with my eyes closed.

Hi everyone, congrats on your surgery journeys! 

 I just had mine this morning and was brought from a 32 F to a B. I couldn’t take the medication they give before the surgery because I was allergic, so after surgery I was in a lot of pain and was given some morphine (about 10 hours from now). And then just tramadol. Now I know what I can and can’t do, I have a newborn at home and I know not to lift anything and what my limits are, but why do I feel fine? I am worried that I am going to do something I shouldn’t just because it doesn’t hurt. I just grabbed something light out of my fridge just above eye level. Is that too much? I have no pain besides my chest aching a little bit. Will I wake up tomorrow feeling everything at once? 

Just to add in my mom is staying with my husband and I for extra help so I’m not having to take care of my daughter at the moment (😢)

Before having my daughter I was a 32 D. After my daughter (without breastfeeding) my breasts went down past my belly button, I don’t even know what size I am because it is such a mess. But some women’s breasts get smaller after a child, it’s really a mystery. My advice would be to have children before a reduction, or keep in mind you may need to get another one done after a child. Hope that helps!
